description: A whole mod list or modpack checked against the Modkeel lab at once: every pair in it that clashed, the mods whose jar crashed, the pairs that ran together, and the mods the lab has no data on. Use it for "will these mods work together?" or before updating a pack; for two mods, check_mod_pair is enough. Takes up to 300 mod ids (from names, search_mods first; unknown ids just land in untested_mods). With mc, only runs on that version count, and each crashed mod also gets the author's current build for it, since the crash is about the exact file the lab ran. verdict is problems_found when anything clashed or crashed, else no_known_problem, which is not a guarantee: pairs.tested out of pairs.total says how much of the list the lab covered.

mc.description: Minecraft version to narrow the answer to, e.g. 1.21.1, 1.20.1 or 26.2. Omit it to get every version the lab ran; with it, only runs on exactly that version count.

mod_ids.description: Lowercase mod ids as the loader knows them, e.g. ["sodium", "iris", "create"]. The ids of a mods folder's jars work.

name: check_mod_list

clashes.description: Pairs in the list that clashed in a lab run.

detail.description: What the lab saw, in words.

source.description: Which lab check produced the run.

crashed.description: Mods whose jar crashed in a lab run: that exact file (runs[].file).

current.description: With mc: the author's current build for it. newer_build: another file than the one that crashed, not run by the lab yet.

detail.description: What the lab saw, in words.

source.description: Which lab check produced the run.

data.description: Snapshot date and license of the lab data; attribute when quoting.

next_step.description: With mc and crashed mods: what to install or leave out, for the player.

ran_together.description: Pairs in the list seen working together.

untested_mods.description: No lab data: unknown, not broken.
